text:
Daniil Tarasov has been the best goalie in the league per minute this season by our numbers, and he has a 3-3-2 record to show for it.

He has saved 9.6 goals more than the shots he faced usually allow (goals saved above expected), the top rate among goalies with 150 shots, on a .931 save percentage. Only one goalie has added more wins with his saves. Two shutouts tell part of it, Montreal on Oct. 10 and Tampa Bay on Nov. 14; after the second, Prashanth Iyer of Expected By Whom posted that he "Kept the Wings in it until they picked up their game in the 2nd period." The rest is the hard stuff: .821 on high-danger shots against a league .685.

Now the caution. Nine games is a small sample for a goalie, and our talent range still puts his true save rate near league average. Last season we had him 2.8 goals below expected in 33 games, though Evolving-Hockey's model was far kinder (plus 12.1 on their scale). Watch the workload: every start that looks like this makes Detroit's crease harder to take from him.
